# DotOS v3.0.0

The biggest release yet — a reworked menu, a Favorites page you build yourself,
an Android-style quick-settings shade, and a lot of polish. The watch firmware
and the companion app share one version number: install **DotOS Phone Link
v3.0.0** on the phone alongside this.

## Flash
Open the one-click web flasher (link below) in Chrome or Edge and click **Install**,
or download the four `.bin` files and `DotOS-v3.0.0-flasher.html` from the assets.
Copy `dotos-v3.0.0-sdcard.zip` to the SD card root for the wallpapers and assets.
Your saved settings (step goal, vibration, favorites, …) now live on the SD card,
so they survive this flash.

## What's new
- **Favorites page** — swipe right on the watch face to reach a page of app
  shortcuts you choose yourself. Tap **Edit** to tick the apps you want; the grid
  and your choices are saved to the SD card.
- **Reworked Apps menu** — tiles reordered (Time & Clock, Notifications, then Apps,
  Music, Health, Tracking, Defense, Offense) with a new **Comms** category grouping
  Meshtastic, Pager and LoRa APRS. A sticky **gear** button, pinned bottom-right, is
  always there to open Settings.
- **Quick-settings shade** — swipe down for an Android-style panel over your
  notifications: **brightness** and **music-volume** sliders, plus pills for
  Bluetooth, USB mount and the connected phone platform.
- **Health tile** — a heart tile in the menu opens the Health screen in one tap.
- **Screenshot feedback** — a capture now flashes the screen, buzzes, and shows a
  confirming toast. Hold to capture is now a 5-second press.
- **Consistent navigation** — swiping right always steps back one screen, anywhere
  on the watch.
- **Settings, redesigned** — collapsible sections, accent-coloured switches and
  calmer sliders. Show Day / Show Date moved in next to the watch face options; the
  Dim Timer now tops out at a sensible 60 s.

## Fixes & under the hood
- **Battery** — the watch now measures its own drain rate, and relaxes the phone
  link while the display is off to save power.
- **Separate vibration controls** — "Vibration" governs notification buzzes;
  a new "Touch feedback" control governs touch vibration. Both persist to SD.
- **Removed clutter** — the Matrix background and Wallpaper features and other dead
  or duplicated pieces are gone, and the settings list is laid out cleanly.
- **Icon polish** — redrawn Comms, Defense and Health icons; assorted layout fixes
  (boot rows, the gear, labels).

Not every change is reflected in these notes; see the commit history for the full list.
